summary: Dimenhydrinate is a salt of the sedating H1-antihistamine diphenhydramine with 8-chlorotheophylline, used as an OTC antiemetic and antivertigo agent to prevent and treat the nausea, vomiting and dizziness of motion sickness. It works mainly through central anticholinergic and antihistaminic effects on the vestibular system. It causes drowsiness, has anticholinergic cautions, and should not be used in children under 2 years unless directed by a doctor.
indications: Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting and dizziness associated with motion sickness

moa: Dimenhydrinate dissociates into diphenhydramine (the active moiety) and 8-chlorotheophylline. Diphenhydramine is a first-generation H1-antihistamine with central anticholinergic activity; it depresses hyperstimulated vestibular function and acts on the chemoreceptor trigger zone and vomiting center to prevent motion-induced nausea and vomiting. The 8-chlorotheophylline component is added to counter excessive drowsiness.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine or related antihistamines

preg: Ask a health professional before use in pregnancy. It has long been used for nausea/vomiting in pregnancy but should be used only when needed and under guidance.
lact: Ask a health professional before use while breastfeeding. Small amounts pass into milk; sedating antihistamines may reduce milk supply and cause infant drowsiness/irritability.

missed: As this is usually taken as needed, take a dose when needed for symptoms. If on a schedule, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next - then skip it; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose causes anticholinergic toxicity (dry flushed skin, dilated pupils, fever, urinary retention), CNS depression or excitation, hallucinations and, in severe cases, seizures, arrhythmias and coma; can be fatal especially in children. Treatment is supportive - control seizures and hyperthermia, monitor cardiac rhythm; get emergency help or contact a poison control center.
